name: Persistence via scheduled task
summary: An intruder stages a script in ProgramData and registers a scheduled task so it runs at every logon. All steps are stubs that only write marker files.
objectives: Walk through how scheduled-task persistence looks on a host.
Identify which logs and artifacts would show each stage.
Agree who would detect it, how fast, and what the response would be.

parameters.name: ArtifactFolder
parameters.description: Folder under %ProgramData% where stand-in artifacts are written. Each session gets its own subfolder.

steps.title: Stage a stand-in script in ProgramData
facilitatorNotes: Setting: the intruder already has a foothold as a standard user and drops a script into a world-writable folder.
Ask: would anything alert on a new script file in ProgramData? Who would see it?
Ask: do we collect file-creation events on workstations, and how long do we keep them?

steps.title: Register a scheduled task that runs the script at logon
facilitatorNotes: Setting: the intruder registers a task with an innocent-looking name so the script survives reboots.
Ask: is task-creation auditing (Security 4698) enabled? Is the TaskScheduler Operational log collected centrally?
Ask: how would an analyst tell this task apart from legitimate updater tasks?

steps.title: The task fires and runs the script
facilitatorNotes: Setting: the user logs on the next morning; the task fires and runs the script.
Ask: what process lineage would we expect to see, and would the EDR flag it?
Ask: once detected, what are the containment and eradication steps, and who owns them?
